messages:
anya: Quick q — proposal for SDK/API headers to steer smart routing and to help debugging fallbacks. Thinking: headers x-redwood-region, x-redwood-tier-override (dev/test only), x-redwood-routing-debug (trace|on). Also a console-only simulate param. Example curl: 

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n     -H "x-redwood-region: eu-west-1" \n     -H "x-redwood-tier-override: dedicated-test" \n     -H "x-redwood-routing-debug: trace" \n     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

We need decisions on: security/entitlements, telemetry fields, and whether SDKs expose an allowFallback flag. Thoughts?

mike: +1 for headers, but strongly prefer we gate tier overrides behind account entitlements. No customer should use tier_override to bypass quotas. For region header: obey if customer has region rights and data residency allows. If not allowed, ignore header and log reason.

sophie: From SDK DX we can do: 

const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey })
const resp = await client.generate({
  prompt,
  routing: { regionHint: 'eu-west-1', allowFallback: true, debug: true }
})

SDK should warn when allowFallback=false because that causes hard errors on fallback. Console UX: add a "Simulate routing" toggle per-route that calls the same path with simulate_routing=true and shows predicted route + cost estimate.

jacob: Security/compliance check: tier_override is risky. Proposal: only accept it when API key has scope "routing:override" (internal/enterprise dev keys). Always emit audit log entry: { actor, api_key_id, header_values, decision_reason }. Also debug header should be limited to internal keys or flagged dev keys — otherwise too noisy.

deploy-bot: deploy: feature-flag routing-headers v2 -> canary succeeded :rocket:

anya: Also thinking about model variant fallback ordering. Proposal: 1) pinned version (if requested) 2) same-arch quantized cheaper variant in same region 3) same model family in nearest region (if residency allowed) 4) global fallback model (small/cheap)

Would be useful to support an SDK flag allowFallback:false so caller can force an error instead of fallback. Example response when fallback blocked: {"error": "fallback_blocked", "message": "requested region unavailable and allowFallback=false"}

mike: agree on allowFallback default true. If allowFallback=false, I think we should return 409 or 424? 503 feels generic. Suggest 409 with structured body including routing.reason and routing.possible_alternatives. Also enforce that simulation requests never consume customer quota (mark simulated=true).

sophie: Telemetry needs these tags on every request: routing.requested_region, routing.effective_region, routing.variant_chain (array as CSV), routing.simulated (true/false), routing.decision_trace_id. Expose these in per-route dashboards and a small "routing waterfall" in Console that shows where time/cost comes from. Simulate mode populates a table of probable failovers + delta tokens/cost.

jacob: Implementation note: server must validate headers against account metadata and write a single-line audit log for sysadmins: 

AUDIT routing header: account=acct_123 api_key=key_456 actor=anya headers="x-redwood-region=eu-west-1,x-redwood-tier-override=..." decision=IGNORED(reason=quota_not_allowed) trace=rt-7890

Also: limit debug traces to 1 request/sec per key to avoid perf impact.

anya: Ok, I'll draft an API contract PR with header names "x-redwood-region", "x-redwood-tier-override", "x-redwood-routing-debug" and a query param simulate_routing=true for console-only calls. Will include allowFallback and clear error codes + telemetry field names. I'll open PR and tag @mike @sophie @jacob for review. Thanks :thumbsup:
